findings.expected: Use a French banner image (e.g. banner-fr.png) reading « Un financement adapté à vos projets — Taux concurrentiels. Modalités claires. Aucune surprise. »
findings.description: The French home page shows the English banner image with English text "Financing that fits your plans / Competitive rates. Clear terms. No surprises."
The footer copyright notice is in English on French pages (shared footer).
The subtitle uses "tu" while the title right above and the rest of the site use "vous".
"Appliquer pour" is an anglicism (calque of "apply for"); the correct French is "faire une demande de prêt" / "demander un prêt".
The required-field error for "Nom complet" is in English on the French form, while the other fields' errors are translated.
"e-mail" is not the Quebec French term; fr-CA uses "courriel" (OQLF recommendation).

findings.observed: Merci. Votre demande pour {montant} a été reçue.
findings.expected: Merci. Votre demande de 15 000,50 $ a été reçue.
findings.description: The confirmation message shows the raw template variable {montant} instead of the amount; the French placeholder name was likely translated so it no longer matches the variable.

findings.expected: Parse the amount with fr-CA conventions on the French form (space as thousands separator, comma as decimal separator).
findings.description: On the French form, a valid amount typed in Canadian French format (15 000,50 or 15000,50) is rejected as out of range; only the English format 15000.50 is accepted, so French users cannot submit with their normal number format.
"Pay later" is translated as "Payer maintenant" (pay now), the opposite meaning, contradicting the help text about a deferred first payment.
The estimated monthly payment uses English currency formatting on the French page instead of fr-CA format (comma decimal, $ after the amount).

findings.observed: Aucune accusation pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.expected: Aucuns frais ne s'appliquent en cas de remboursement anticipé.
findings.description: "Charges" (fees) was translated as "accusation" (criminal charge/accusation), which is wrong in a financial context.

findings.expected: Taux variable de 5,2 %, sous réserve de l'approbation du crédit.
findings.description: The French rate note drops the condition "subject to credit approval", presenting the rate as unconditional.

findings.expected: Use a French version of promo-a showing « Taux variable : 5,2 % ».
findings.description: The French page shows a different promo image advertising a fixed rate of 4.9%, while the English shows a variable rate of 5.2% and the French alt text and page say variable 5.2%.
The verb "Close" was translated as the adjective "Proche" (near), which is meaningless as a close-dialog action.
"Balance" is an anglicism for an account balance; the correct banking term in French is "solde".
In French, zero takes the singular; the English plural rule was applied to the French string.
The transactions table heading is left in English on the French dashboard.
Transaction dates on the French dashboard use the US MM/DD/YYYY format, which is ambiguous and not a fr-CA convention; the English page uses ISO.
A bank "statement" is a "relevé"; "déclaration" means a declaration (e.g. tax return), which is wrong in context.
The "Estimer un nouveau prêt" link on the French dashboard points to the English calculator, switching the user to English.
The French application confirmation page declares its document language as English, while other French pages declare fr-CA.

findings.expected: Let the button grow with its content (remove fixed width / overflow hidden), or shorten to « Soumettre la demande ».
findings.description: The French submit button text is cut off: scrollWidth 290px vs clientWidth 210px with overflow hidden and nowrap, so the end of the label is clipped.
